title: Design System Governance Manifest v2 — contribution, RFCs, review checklist, and deprecation flow
creator: Alex Kim
description: Consolidated, operational-ready governance document for the design system to standardize how new components/tokens are proposed, reviewed, landed, and deprecated. This manifest covers: contribution workflow (templates, branching, Storybook requirements), a lightweight RFC lifecycle for design proposals, a granular review checklist for designers and engineers, token migration strategy (aliases, semantic tokens, token-rename policy), and a clear deprecation policy with timelines and communication templates. The goal is to reduce friction for contributors while preventing surprise regressions in production apps and keeping the token surface manageable.

review_checklist: Design acceptance: Figma component with variants, tokens mapped, interaction specs, and example usage
Accessibility: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text, semantic ARIA roles, keyboard focus, and screen-reader labels verified
API surface: props documented (stable/experimental), default values and deprecation flags included
Performance: snapshot tests for big datasets (tables, charts) and guidelines for virtualization or lazy rendering
Tokens: new tokens must include semantic name, intended usage, and migration plan if replacing an existing token
Storybook: component stories for default, edge-cases, dark mode, and responsive sizes with visual regression capture
Unit & visual tests: Jest/RTL tests for behavior and Chromatic/Storybook visual diffs enabled
Docs: usage examples, migration guide, and code snippets in SDK/MDX docs
Security & privacy: callouts for any components that handle PII or user content
Owners: designate design and engineering owners and rotation cadence (12 months suggested)
rfc_process_summary: We use a staged RFC process for non-trivial changes: 1) Idea (short pitch, 1 page) 2) Draft RFC (detailed design, alternatives, migration plan, impact analysis) 3) Review window (2 weeks cross-team) 4) Signoff (Design + Eng + PM) 5) Implementation tracked via Linear issues. RFCs must include automated test requirements and a rollback plan.
token_migration_plan: Prefer semantic tokens (eg --color-brand-foreground) over physical tokens (eg --blue-600)
Introduce new semantic token as additive; do not remove old token for at least two minor releases
Implement a token alias layer in CSS/JS that maps deprecated names to current tokens at runtime
Provide codemods for common frameworks (React, Solid) to assist bulk renames
Document migration guide with sample PR and storybook before/after snapshots
Critical constraint: any token rename that affects default visual weight triggers an accessibility re-check
deprecation_policy_summary: Deprecation happens in three phases: Announcement (T0) with migration docs and Slack + changelog entries; Soft-deprecation (T+1 release) where warnings appear in Storybook and console during dev builds; Removal (T+2 release) where the token/component is removed from the library. Enterprise customers will receive a 90-day notice with dedicated migration support. All deprecations must be logged in the Design Deprecation Register.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-team signoff captured in RFC PR and approved by designers and engineers
Automated checks added to CI (Storybook visual diffs and linter rules for token usage)
Migration codemods and a sample migration PR exist for non-trivial token/component renames
Documentation pages updated and linked from the console onboarding flow
Owners and rotation schedule published in the team handbook
open_questions: Should we enforce token naming conventions with a pre-commit hook or allow opt-out for experimental branches?
What SLA should we promise for rolling back a breaking change introduced by a component release?
How to surface component-level telemetry (errors/latency) without creating privacy exposures for customer content?
